doc.title: Richard Wyands interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 7, 2002

title: Playing in strip clubs
summary: Continuous music, stock arrangements and staggered breaks in small bands behind strippers.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: What kind of tunes, at that time, worked in the strip club?
Mostly standards. We got away with that.

Yeah. Some of the typical strip type tunes, but this was way back then in the 40s, we’re talking about late 40s I guess. Some of the strippers had their own music, they brought in some of these old stock arrangements. There was only a four-piece band, four or five piece band, how much could we play? And the piano would be stacked with music, I remember that much. And the music had to be continuous. The band never stopped playing. So we’d take our breaks individually.
No intermissions. Because there were a lot of strippers. Some of the clubs had maybe ten and so they’d come out.
So from — like what time would you start?

Eight o’clock until sometimes two A.M. And one by one the guys would get up and take a little break, 15 minutes or so. It must have been — I mean so weird, okay now there’s going to be no drums for a little while.
So you’d have bass and sax and drums maybe or something like that?
Well sometimes one of the horn players would double on piano and play enough to get by, you know, play some chords.
That’s interesting. You probably got to see all kinds of acts too.
